papers.title: BioMedGraphica: An All-in-One Platform for Joint Textual Biomedical Prior Knowledge and Numeric Graph Generation
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multi-omics data analysis is essential for scientific discovery in precision medicine. However, translating analysis results of omics data analysis into novel scientific hypotheses remains a significant challenge. Human experts must manually review analysis results and generate new hypotheses based on extensive and inter-connected biomedical prior knowledge, which is subjective and not scalable. While large language models (LLMs) can accelerate the discovery, their reasoning improves when grounded in structured, auditable and comprehensive biomedical prior knowledge. However, biomedical knowledge is scattered across heterogeneous databases that use diverse and inconsistent nomenclature systems, making it difficult to integrate resources into a unified format for scalable analysis. This fragmentation limits the ability of AI systems to fully leverage biomedical data for scientific discovery. Results We developed BioMedGraphica, a novel all-in-one platform that harmonizes fragmented biomedical resources by integrating 11 entity types and 30 relation types from 43 databases into a unified textual prior knowledge graph containing 2,306,921 entities and 27,232,091 relations. In addition, we present a novel text-numeric-graph (TNG) data structure concept, where textual information captures prior biological knowledge (e.g., transcription start sites, functions, mechanisms), numeric values represent quantitative biomedical features, and the integrated relations can help uncover mechanisms. By bridging prior knowledge with user-specific data, TNG is a novel and ideal data structure for developing novel graph analysis models. Availability and implementation The code is available at: https://github.com/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica and BioMedGraphica knowledge graph database can be downloaded from huggingface dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Multi-omics data analysis is essential for scientific discovery in precision medicine. However, translating analysis results of omics data analysis into novel scientific hypotheses remains a significant challenge. Human experts must manually review analysis results and generate new hypotheses based on extensive and inter-connected biomedical prior knowledge, which is subjective and not scalable. While large language models (LLMs) can accelerate the discovery, their reasoning improves when grounded in structured, auditable and comprehensive biomedical prior knowledge. However, biomedical knowledge is scattered across heterogeneous databases that use diverse and inconsistent nomenclature systems, making it difficult to integrate resources into a unified format for scalable analysis. This fragmentation limits the ability of AI systems to fully leverage biomedical data for scientific discovery.

RESULTS: We developed BioMedGraphica, a novel all-in-one platform that harmonizes fragmented biomedical resources by integrating 11 entity types and 30 relation types from 43 databases into a unified textual prior knowledge graph containing 2,306,921 entities and 27,232,091 relations. In addition, we present a novel text-numeric-graph (TNG) data structure concept, where textual information captures prior biological knowledge (e.g., transcription start sites, functions, mechanisms), numeric values represent quantitative biomedical features, and the integrated relations can help uncover mechanisms. By bridging prior knowledge with user-specific data, TNG is a novel and ideal data structure for developing novel graph analysis models.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The code is available at: https://github.com/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica and BioMedGraphica knowledge graph database can be downloaded from huggingface dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.llm_title_zh: BioMedGraphica：一个集文本形式的生物医学先验知识与数值图表生成功能于一体的综合平台
papers.llm_title_bilingual: BioMedGraphica：一个集文本形式的生物医学先验知识与数值图表生成功能于一体的综合平台 / BioMedGraphica: An All-in-One Platform for Joint Textual Biomedical Prior Knowledge and Numeric Graph Generation
papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：多组学数据分析对于精准医学领域的科学研究而言至关重要。
llm_highlights_zh: 然而，将组学数据分析的结果转化为新的科学假说仍然是一项巨大的挑战。
人类专家必须手动审查分析结果，并根据丰富的、相互关联的生物医学知识来提出新的假设，这一过程具有主观性且难以实现规模化操作。
虽然大型语言模型能够加速研究进程，但当它们的推理过程基于结构化、可审核且全面的生物医学先验知识时，其推理能力才会得到进一步提升。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
多组学数据分析对于精准医学领域的科学研究至关重要。然而，将这类分析结果转化为新的科学假说仍面临重大挑战——人类专家需要手动审查分析结果，并基于庞大的、相互关联的生物医学知识来提出新假设，这一过程具有主观性且难以实现规模化处理。虽然大型语言模型能够加速这一发现过程，但它们的推理能力只有在依托结构化、可验证且全面的生物医学知识时才能得到提升。然而，现有的生物医学知识分散在各种异构数据库中，这些数据库使用着多种不一致的命名系统，因此很难将这些资源整合成统一的格式以进行大规模分析。这种数据碎片化的现状限制了人工智能技术在科学发现中的应用潜力。  

**研究结果**  
我们开发了BioMedGraphica这一一体化平台，它通过整合来自43个数据库的11种实体类型和30种关系类型，构建了一个包含2,306,921个实体及27,232,091条关系的统一文本型知识图谱，从而有效解决了生物医学数据碎片化的问题。此外，我们还提出了一种新的文本-数值-图形结合的数据结构模型——TNG：其中文本信息用于表达生物学基础知识（如转录起始位点、功能机制等），数值则代表定量化的生物医学特征，而这些整合在一起的关系有助于揭示各种生理机制。通过将先验知识与用户特定的数据相结合，TNG成为开发高效图谱分析模型的理想数据结构。  

**代码与资源获取**  
相关代码可访问以下链接下载：https://github.com/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica；BioMedGraphica知识图谱数据库也可从HuggingFace数据集平台获取：https://huggingface.co/datasets/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica

papers.title: Brightness demixing for simultaneous multi-target imaging in 3D single-molecule localization microscopy
papers.summary: Brightness demixing is a method for simultaneously detecting different fluorophores in single-molecule localization microscopy based on their brightness rather than their spectral properties. As this approach allows imaging in a single channel, it simplifies and speeds up the imaging of multiple targets

all_papers.title: BioMedGraphica: An All-in-One Platform for Joint Textual Biomedical Prior Knowledge and Numeric Graph Generation
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multi-omics data analysis is essential for scientific discovery in precision medicine. However, translating analysis results of omics data analysis into novel scientific hypotheses remains a significant challenge. Human experts must manually review analysis results and generate new hypotheses based on extensive and inter-connected biomedical prior knowledge, which is subjective and not scalable. While large language models (LLMs) can accelerate the discovery, their reasoning improves when grounded in structured, auditable and comprehensive biomedical prior knowledge. However, biomedical knowledge is scattered across heterogeneous databases that use diverse and inconsistent nomenclature systems, making it difficult to integrate resources into a unified format for scalable analysis. This fragmentation limits the ability of AI systems to fully leverage biomedical data for scientific discovery. Results We developed BioMedGraphica, a novel all-in-one platform that harmonizes fragmented biomedical resources by integrating 11 entity types and 30 relation types from 43 databases into a unified textual prior knowledge graph containing 2,306,921 entities and 27,232,091 relations. In addition, we present a novel text-numeric-graph (TNG) data structure concept, where textual information captures prior biological knowledge (e.g., transcription start sites, functions, mechanisms), numeric values represent quantitative biomedical features, and the integrated relations can help uncover mechanisms. By bridging prior knowledge with user-specific data, TNG is a novel and ideal data structure for developing novel graph analysis models. Availability and implementation The code is available at: https://github.com/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica and BioMedGraphica knowledge graph database can be downloaded from huggingface dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica
all_papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Multi-omics data analysis is essential for scientific discovery in precision medicine. However, translating analysis results of omics data analysis into novel scientific hypotheses remains a significant challenge. Human experts must manually review analysis results and generate new hypotheses based on extensive and inter-connected biomedical prior knowledge, which is subjective and not scalable. While large language models (LLMs) can accelerate the discovery, their reasoning improves when grounded in structured, auditable and comprehensive biomedical prior knowledge. However, biomedical knowledge is scattered across heterogeneous databases that use diverse and inconsistent nomenclature systems, making it difficult to integrate resources into a unified format for scalable analysis. This fragmentation limits the ability of AI systems to fully leverage biomedical data for scientific discovery.

RESULTS: We developed BioMedGraphica, a novel all-in-one platform that harmonizes fragmented biomedical resources by integrating 11 entity types and 30 relation types from 43 databases into a unified textual prior knowledge graph containing 2,306,921 entities and 27,232,091 relations. In addition, we present a novel text-numeric-graph (TNG) data structure concept, where textual information captures prior biological knowledge (e.g., transcription start sites, functions, mechanisms), numeric values represent quantitative biomedical features, and the integrated relations can help uncover mechanisms. By bridging prior knowledge with user-specific data, TNG is a novel and ideal data structure for developing novel graph analysis models.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The code is available at: https://github.com/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica and BioMedGraphica knowledge graph database can be downloaded from huggingface dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.llm_title_zh: BioMedGraphica：一个集文本形式的生物医学先验知识与数值图表生成功能于一体的综合平台
all_papers.llm_title_bilingual: BioMedGraphica：一个集文本形式的生物医学先验知识与数值图表生成功能于一体的综合平台 / BioMedGraphica: An All-in-One Platform for Joint Textual Biomedical Prior Knowledge and Numeric Graph Generation
all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：多组学数据分析对于精准医学领域的科学研究而言至关重要。
llm_highlights_zh: 然而，将组学数据分析的结果转化为新的科学假说仍然是一项巨大的挑战。
人类专家必须手动审查分析结果，并根据丰富的、相互关联的生物医学知识来提出新的假设，这一过程具有主观性且难以实现规模化操作。
虽然大型语言模型能够加速研究进程，但当它们的推理过程基于结构化、可审核且全面的生物医学先验知识时，其推理能力才会得到进一步提升。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
多组学数据分析对于精准医学领域的科学研究至关重要。然而，将这类分析结果转化为新的科学假说仍面临重大挑战——人类专家需要手动审查分析结果，并基于庞大的、相互关联的生物医学知识来提出新假设，这一过程具有主观性且难以实现规模化处理。虽然大型语言模型能够加速这一发现过程，但它们的推理能力只有在依托结构化、可验证且全面的生物医学知识时才能得到提升。然而，现有的生物医学知识分散在各种异构数据库中，这些数据库使用着多种不一致的命名系统，因此很难将这些资源整合成统一的格式以进行大规模分析。这种数据碎片化的现状限制了人工智能技术在科学发现中的应用潜力。  

**研究结果**  
我们开发了BioMedGraphica这一一体化平台，它通过整合来自43个数据库的11种实体类型和30种关系类型，构建了一个包含2,306,921个实体及27,232,091条关系的统一文本型知识图谱，从而有效解决了生物医学数据碎片化的问题。此外，我们还提出了一种新的文本-数值-图形结合的数据结构模型——TNG：其中文本信息用于表达生物学基础知识（如转录起始位点、功能机制等），数值则代表定量化的生物医学特征，而这些整合在一起的关系有助于揭示各种生理机制。通过将先验知识与用户特定的数据相结合，TNG成为开发高效图谱分析模型的理想数据结构。  

**代码与资源获取**  
相关代码可访问以下链接下载：https://github.com/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica；BioMedGraphica知识图谱数据库也可从HuggingFace数据集平台获取：https://huggingface.co/datasets/FuhaiLiAiLab/BioMedGraphica
